title: Token transfer totals are summed independently by the Governance Point and Technical Point, and only after the sheet is complete
content:
A.1.10.2.4.3.2.3 requires that "the total amount of token transfers must always be summed up in the Executive Sheet. **The Governance Point and Technical Point independently sum up the value.**" It closes with a sequencing rule: "All summations must occur only after the Executive Sheet is complete to avoid missing any transfers."

A total computed once is a convenience. A total computed twice by different parties is a control: it cannot catch an error both make, but it reliably catches the dominant failure mode here — one person mistyping, misreading or overlooking a row. Disagreement between two numbers is loud in a way that a single wrong number never is.

The timing clause defends against the subtler failure. A total computed mid-assembly is correct for a sheet that no longer exists, and it then looks like verification while covering nothing added afterwards. A stale checksum is worse than none, because it converts an unchecked sheet into an apparently checked one.

The pattern is the same one the Atlas uses for novel-item design (both Spell Teams must agree, A.1.10.2.3.3.2.3) and for forum-post confirmation: where an error is cheap to make, expensive to suffer and hard to see, Sky buys a second independent computation rather than asking for more care on the first.
description: Duplicate arithmetic by two parties turns a silent transcription error into a visible mismatch; deferring summation until the sheet is final prevents a stale total from validating a changed sheet.
